rows.label: Concept
rows.text: Viruses are acellular, obligate intracellular parasites that contain either DNA or RNA enclosed in a protein capsid (and sometimes a lipid envelope). They cannot replicate outside a host cell and hijack host machinery. The T4 bacteriophage lytic cycle (adsorption, injection, replication, assembly, release) is the NEB model.…

rows.label: Formula
rows.text:
Virus = Nucleic acid (DNA or RNA) + Capsid (protein) [+ Envelope (lipid + glycoprotein)]
Lytic cycle: Adsorption → Penetration (injection) → Biosynthesis → Assembly → Release
Lysogenic cycle: Prophage integration → Replication with host → Induction → Lytic cycle

rows.label: Conditions
rows.text: Viruses are NOT living organisms: they lack metabolism, cannot reproduce outside a host, and are not made of cells.  ·  A virus has EITHER DNA or RNA, never both (with rare exceptions like some retroviruses that convert RNA to DNA).

rows.label: Special cases
rows.text: NEB expects a detailed T4 phage diagram and the 5-step lytic cycle.  ·  The "are viruses alive?" debate is a favourite exam discussion; present both arguments.

rows.label: Solved
rows.text: Worked: identify given → pick sub-concept → apply standard form → check units / edges.  ·  T4 bacteriophage — DNA virus, infects E. coli; lytic cycle model.

rows.label: Study notes
rows.text: Viruses: acellular, obligate intracellular parasites; not classified in any kingdom; consist of a nucleic acid core (DNA or RNA) + protein coat (capsid); some have a lipid envelope.  ·  Structure: capsomeres (protein subunits of capsid); bacteriophages have a head (icosahedral) + tail; animal viruses may have an envelope with glycoprotein spikes.  ·  Types by nucleic acid: DNA viruses (e.g., T4 phage, smallpox) and RNA viruses (e.g., influenza, HIV, SARS-CoV-2).

rows.label: More ideas
rows.text: Gene therapy applications  ·  Viruses are acellular, obligate intracellular parasites.  ·  Structure: nucleic acid + capsid (+ envelope in some).

rows.label: More ideas
rows.text: DNA or RNA (not both); capsomeres form the capsid.  ·  Bacteriophage: icosahedral head + tail + baseplate + tail fibers.  ·  Lytic cycle: 5 steps, destroys host; Lysogenic: integrates, delays lysis.

rows.label: More ideas
rows.text: Not living: no metabolism, no independent reproduction.  ·  Importance: cause many diseases; used in gene therapy and research.  ·  Bacteriophages infect BACTERIA; animal viruses infect animals; plant viruses infect plants.

rows.label: More ideas
rows.text: The capsid is protein; the core is nucleic acid; the envelope (if present) is lipid + glycoproteins from the host membrane.  ·  Lytic cycle destroys the host cell; lysogenic cycle integrates viral DNA into the host genome (prophage) without immediate lysis.  ·  Viruses are NOT visible under a light microscope; they require an electron microscope (~20–300 nm size).
